input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. ... 28.2 The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum.
input.rationale: Section 28 selects New York law and grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County, which is exactly our preferred position. No arbitration provision appears anywhere in the document (search for "arbitration" returns nothing), so there is no foreign-seat arbitration risk. The pre-filing executive escalation step in 28.2/28.3 (fifteen business days' good-faith meeting) and the carve-out permitting interim injunctive relief in other courts do not displace New York courts and expressly do not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings; noted for information only. No redline required.
